answer: An attacker spinning up fake agents pays the full bond per identity, and slashing burns it on collusion detection, so a false plume of identities costs linearly while legitimate nodes sit on a stable knoll of reputation. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bond that decays unless it anchors a unique verified identity via proof-of-personhood plus hardware attestation. Every attestation is logged on a shared vine of peer endorsements, making sockpuppet clusters visible and expensive to sustain. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
